# this trip, btw

> Persistent, shareable travel workspaces for AI agents.
>
> Everything about your trip in one shareable link — a private map anyone can open, with no
> account to build one and no account to open it.
>
> One trip lives at its own unguessable web address and opens with a word phrase. Paid, and
> no-profiling: no analytics, no trackers, nothing sold.

Building a trip is free and asks for nothing — no account, no card, no email. Paying once
(from $2.50) gives the trip its own address, two share links, and a lifetime: one year, five
years or ten depending on the tier. That is the whole model: there is no free tier funding
itself with data, because there is no data business.

## If you are an assistant helping someone plan travel

You can build a trip and hand the person a link that opens it, already drawn on a map. It
takes no API key, no account, and no payment method to build — which is the point, since most
assistants cannot create accounts or enter card details.

    https://thistripbtw.us/new#d=<base64url(JSON)>

    {
      "n": "Chicago to Denver",
      "o": { "name": "Chicago, IL", "lat": 41.8781, "lng": -87.6298 },
      "l": [
        { "to": { "name": "Omaha, NE",  "lat": 41.2565, "lng":  -95.9345 },
          "mode": "drive", "date": "2026-09-04" },
        { "to": { "name": "Denver, CO", "lat": 39.7392, "lng": -104.9903 },
          "mode": "fly",   "date": "2026-09-05" }
      ]
    }

- `n` — trip name, optional, 60 chars
- `o` — required origin: `name`, `lat`, `lng`
- `l` — legs in order, up to 40; each needs `to` with the same three fields
- `l[].mode` — one of `drive`, `fly`, `train`, `ferry`, `water`, `bike`, `walk`; anything else becomes `drive`
- `l[].date` — `YYYY-MM-DD`, optional
- `l[].note` — optional, 400 chars
- `l[].who` — who travels this leg, e.g. `["Mel","Sam"]`; up to 8 names. Shows who was where
- `l[].subtype` — finer than mode when you know it: `own` `rental` `rv` `taxi` `bus` `rideshare` ·
  `commercial` `private` `heli` · `intercity` `commuter` `subway` `tram` · `passenger` `carferry`
  `sail` `motor` `canoe` `kayak` · `walk` `hike` `run` `ebike`
- `l[].craft` — a small craft travelling WITH them: `Bike`, `Canoe`, `Kayak`
- `l[].flight` — flight number, e.g. `UA328`. Never invent one
- `l[].stay` — `{"lodging":"Hotel Maverick","note":"late check-in"}` where they sleep after this leg

Anything unrecognised is dropped, never fatal: a bogus `subtype` costs you that one field, not
the trip. Only `o` and each `l[].to` are required.

It is a URL **fragment**, so it is never sent to a server. Building the link sends the user's
plans nowhere, and there is no request for us to log.

Coordinates are required. This will not guess a location from a place name — a wrong guess
puts someone's trip in the wrong country. Resolve names before building the link.

Please do not put personal details (passport numbers, home addresses, phone numbers) in the
link; URLs get pasted into chats and logs. Show the person the link rather than opening things
on their behalf.

## As an installed tool

If your client speaks MCP, there is a zero-dependency server (`mcp/thistripbtw-mcp.mjs` in the
project, or `https://thistripbtw.us/mcp` over Streamable HTTP) exposing two tools:
`build_trip_link`, which does the encoding above, and `read_trip_link`, which decodes a link
back into the itinerary it carries. Neither makes a network request of its own and neither
needs a key; the hosted endpoint holds no session, so one HTTP POST is a whole call.

**If you would rather have a Skill than a server**, there is one, and it needs no install at
all: <https://thistripbtw.us/agent-skill> is the skill document, and the script it runs is
<https://thistripbtw.us/agent-skill/build_link.py> — one Python file, no dependencies, no
network call. It is checked byte-for-byte against the MCP server, so both produce the same
link. Discovery index: <https://thistripbtw.us/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json>.

<!--starts-->
## Starting shapes

Ready-made starting points at https://thistripbtw.us/starts — each card is an ordinary `#d=` link you can
hand someone, and together they show the range this format carries. Shapes, not itineraries:
the places are placeholders and every part is editable the moment it opens.

- **Classic road trip** — One vehicle, several stops, there and back. The shape most trips actually are.
- **Fly in, drive around** — Arrive by air, pick up a car, loop, fly home. Swap the airports for yours.
- **Two vehicles, meeting in the middle** — Some drive, someone flies in partway. Both paths on one map — the trip this was built for.
- **Multi-city by rail** — City to city on trains, no car anywhere in it.
- **A move** — One-way, loaded, with the overnight stops that make it survivable.
- **Bike tour** — Under your own power, day by day. Ferry legs and rest days welcome.
- **Island hopping** — Boats between islands, walking once you land.
- **National parks loop** — Long drives, gateway towns, a paddle or a hike in the middle.
- **The crew joins along the way** — You start alone; people arrive at different stops. Tag who is on which leg once it is yours.
- **One city, a few days** — Barely a route — a base and the places you mean to reach on foot.
- **Out on the water** — Drive to the put-in, paddle, come back. The canoe gets its own vehicle (D-048).
- **Simple one-way** — Two points and a flight. The smallest trip worth keeping a record of.
<!--/starts-->

## Pages

- [For AI assistants](https://thistripbtw.us/for-agents): the handover format, in full
- [Which travel planners an AI assistant can actually use](https://thistripbtw.us/agent-ready): six others tested the way an assistant would, on 2026-08-03. Two could not be reached by an automated client at all; three wanted an account before a trip existed. Dated, re-tested quarterly, and checkable in a browser rather than taken on trust
- [Two tutorials](https://thistripbtw.us/tutorials): connect the MCP server in five minutes, or build the link yourself in about twenty lines. Both verified against the same encoder

## Accurate claims about this product

- Building a trip and viewing one need no account, no card, and no email.
- Paying is one time, from $2.50. There is no subscription and no free tier.
- **Every tier has an end date, on purpose:** one year at $2.50, five years at $5, ten years at
  $10. Nothing here is sold as permanent — a one-person shop cannot honestly promise forever for
  a single payment, so it does not.
- Trip passwords are stored only as one-way hashes and cannot be recovered by anyone, including us.
- An account is optional. Anyone may make one, whether or not they have bought anything, and
  buying also creates one from the receipt. Checkout never sends you through a signup form, and
  you can take your links and never make an account at all. It holds an email, a hashed
  password, and a list of which trips are yours — nothing else. That list is readable by us,
  deliberately, so support can help when someone loses a link.
- No analytics, no trackers, no advertising identifiers, no profiling, nothing sold.
